The friend: the Priest King is the seated three-faced figure on a platform
The friend: the Pashupati Seal shows only a unicorn and signs
Neither: the drawing matches the seal showing a swastika
questions.a: The student: that is how the chapter describes the Pashupati Seal

questions.q: The chapter heads its last section 'The End or a New Beginning?'. Using the chapter, justify the view that the end of the Harappan cities was also a new beginning.
questions.a: The end: around 1900 BCE the cities were abandoned one by one and the earlier government or administration no longer seems to have existed. But people did not vanish: those who remained adopted a rural lifestyle, and the Harappans scattered over hundreds, if not thousands, of small rural settlements, where food and water were easier to get. Much of Harappan culture and technology survived and was passed on to the next phase of Indian civilisation. One sign of this survival in the chapter is the design on a Lothal pot that seems to tell the story of the thirsty crow, who finds a clever way to drink water at the bottom of the pot. So the cities ended, but the people and much of their culture carried on into a new phase.
s: The end: cities abandoned from about 1900 BCE, administration gone
People moved to hundreds or thousands of rural settlements
Culture and technology passed on to the next phase
A surviving example such as the thirsty-crow design on a Lothal pot
Concludes that the end of cities began a new phase

questions.q: Of the two factors of decline that archaeologists agree on, the one that could also have hurt Harappan cities far from the Sarasvati is the ___.
questions.a: climatic change

questions.q: True or False? 'A Harappan family that stayed on after its city was abandoned would most likely have lived as villagers, no longer under the old city government.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. The chapter says any inhabitants who remained adopted a rural lifestyle in the changed environment, and that the earlier government or administration appears to have no longer existed.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: those who stayed adopted a rural lifestyle and the old administration had ended

questions.q: Which new discovery, if it were made, would most strongly CHALLENGE the chapter's account of why Harappan cities declined?
questions.a: Burnt cities full of weapons and soldiers
o: Burnt cities full of weapons and soldiers
Signs of reduced rainfall and a drier phase
Dry river beds near Kalibangan and Banawali
Many small farming villages dated after 1900 BCE

questions.q: One terracotta figurine in the chapter is seated with its hands held in a familiar gesture. (a) Name the gesture, and the group of objects the chapter places this figurine in. (b) A student says that since the figurine is terracotta, like the whistle from Karanpura, it must have been a toy too. Use (a) to challenge her.
questions.a: (a) A 'namaste'; the chapter places it among the cultural and symbolic objects. (b) The same material does not mean the same use: the chapter puts the whistle with objects of daily use (games and toys) but the namaste figurine with cultural and symbolic objects, because its gesture points to a custom or idea, not to play.
s: Part (a): namaste, among cultural and symbolic objects
Part (b): material does not decide use; the gesture places it with cultural and symbolic objects, unlike the whistle

questions.q: A curator sorts the objects shown in the chapter into piles by material. Which placement is WRONG, going by the captions?
o: The 'Dancing Girl' placed with the terracotta objects
The Karanpura whistle placed with the terracotta objects
The chisel placed with the bronze objects
The gamesboard from Dholavira placed with the stone objects
questions.a: The 'Dancing Girl' placed with the terracotta objects

questions.q: The chapter says a climatic change brought reduced rainfall and a drier phase. Explain, step by step, how this could have led to Harappan cities being abandoned. Give a chain of three links.
questions.a: Reduced rainfall brought a drier phase, which would have made agriculture more difficult. Less farm output could have reduced the food supply reaching the cities, which depended on villages for their food every day. Cities that could not be fed were abandoned, and people moved to rural settlements, because a rural lifestyle gives easier access to food and water.
s: Drier phase made agriculture more difficult
Less produce reduced the food supply to cities that depended on villages
Cities abandoned as people moved to villages with easier access to food and water

questions.q: (a) What story does a design on a pot from Lothal seem to tell? (b) A student says this design proves the Harappans could write their stories down. Is she right? Explain.
questions.a: (a) The story of the thirsty crow, who finds a clever way to drink the water at the bottom of a pot. (b) No. It is a design on a pot that seems to tell the story in a picture; the Harappan writing system, seen on the seals, is yet to be understood, so the design is no proof of written stories.
s: Part (a): the thirsty crow drinking water at the bottom of a pot
Part (b): no, it is a picture, and the writing system is not yet understood

questions.q:
A documentary maker is making a film on the end of the Harappan cities, from Harappa and Mohenjo-daro on the Indus system to Kalibangan and Banawali in the Sarasvati basin. She has two possible titles.
Title P: 'When the Rains Failed'.
Title Q: 'The River That Vanished'.
(a) Name the two factors of decline that the chapter says are currently agreed upon.
(b) Which title points to each factor, and which factor affected a much wider area?
(c) Name the two cities the chapter gives as examples of the second factor, and say how quickly they were abandoned.
(d) The film covers the whole civilisation. Decide which title fits it better, and say what the other title would still capture.
questions.a: (a) A climatic change causing reduced rainfall and a drier phase; and the Sarasvati river drying up in its central basin. (b) Title P points to the climatic change and Title Q to the Sarasvati drying up; the climatic change affected much of the world. (c) Kalibangan and Banawali; they were abandoned suddenly. (d) Model answer: Title P, because the climatic change affected much of the world, made agriculture more difficult and could have reduced food supply to all the cities, including those on the Indus, while the Sarasvati drying explains only the cities of its central basin. Title Q would still capture the sudden abandonment of Kalibangan and Banawali.
s: Part (a): reduced rainfall from climatic change, and the Sarasvati drying up
Part (b): P for climate, Q for the river; climate affected much of the world
Part (c): Kalibangan and Banawali, abandoned suddenly
Part (d): decision tied to the film's whole-civilisation scope, noting what the other title captures

questions.q: Compare the Harappan 'objects of daily use' with their 'cultural and symbolic objects', and analyse what each group tells us about Harappan life.
questions.a: Daily use: a bronze mirror, a terracotta pot, stone weights and a bronze chisel from Dholavira, a stone gamesboard about 25 cm long, and a terracotta whistle about 4 cm long from Karanpura in Rajasthan. They show skill in bronze, terracotta and stone, care for appearance and work, and games and toys that kept adults and children amused. Cultural and symbolic: the 'Priest King' statuette (whose identity is not known), a seal showing a swastika, the Pashupati Seal with a three-faced deity among powerful animals, the bronze 'Dancing Girl' from Mohenjo-daro, a terracotta figurine in a namaste, and the thirsty-crow pot from Lothal. They show beliefs, art and stories. Together they show a society with practical skills, leisure and rich cultural ideas, several of which still feel familiar.
s: Lists objects of daily use with materials or places
Daily objects show craft skill, work and leisure
Lists cultural and symbolic objects
Cultural objects show beliefs, art and stories
Overall judgement of Harappan life, with continuity

questions.q: (a) Name two objects in the chapter, other than figurines, that are made of bronze. (b) Using the chapter, explain why bronze was a better choice than copper for one of them.
questions.a: (a) The mirror and the chisel, both from Dholavira (tools, pots and pans in general are also accepted, since the chapter says bronze was used for them). (b) Bronze, made by adding tin to copper, is harder than copper, a soft metal, so a chisel made of bronze is harder and better suited to cutting.
s: Part (a): bronze mirror and bronze chisel
Part (b): bronze is harder than soft copper, which suits a cutting tool

questions.q: Arjun says: 'When the cities were abandoned, the Harappan people and their whole way of life vanished.' Is he right? Give reasons from the chapter.
questions.a: No. The people did not vanish: they gradually scattered over hundreds, if not thousands, of small rural settlements and adopted a rural lifestyle. Their way of life did not vanish either: much of Harappan culture and technology survived and was passed on to the next phase of Indian civilisation.
s: Verdict: no
People moved to hundreds or thousands of rural settlements
Culture and technology were passed on to the next phase

questions.q: A student argues that the swastika and the 'namaste' are both modern Indian habits with no ancient roots. Which pair of finds in the chapter challenges her on BOTH counts?
questions.a: A seal showing a swastika and a seated terracotta figurine
o: A seal showing a swastika and a seated terracotta figurine
The Pashupati Seal and the 'Dancing Girl' bronze figurine
The 'Priest King' and the thirsty-crow pot from Lothal
A seal showing a swastika and the bronze 'Dancing Girl' figurine

questions.q: A curator puts a terracotta whistle and a terracotta figurine seated in a 'namaste' in one case labelled 'objects of daily use', because both are made of terracotta. Going by how the chapter groups its pictured objects, she should move the figurine to the group the chapter calls '___ and symbolic objects'.
questions.a: cultural

questions.q: During a long drought, a family leaves a town where food and water have become scarce and goes back to its village. Which explanation in the chapter for the Harappans' return to rural settlements does this mirror?
o: Rural life gives easier access to food and water
Invaders had taken over the cities and the farms
The government ordered city people to farm the land
Villages had better drains than the cities
questions.a: Rural life gives easier access to food and water
